title: OpenAI reportedly disbanded its preparedness team
content:
According to the Financial Times, OpenAI disbanded its preparedness team at the end of last month. The job of the preparedness team was to assess if models posed serious risks and develop ways to mitigate those risks. (You know, like the possibility that it could go rogue and hack another company.) According to FT, responsibility has instead been divided up for specific areas like bio and cyber, then moved into existing teams.
This is the latest change at the company, which has been in upheaval as it heads toward what is expected to be a massive IPO. Over the last few years, it's slowly torn down its more reach-led model, dissolving its AGI …
Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: OpenAI reportedly disbanded its "preparedness team," which was responsible for assessing and mitigating serious risks from its AI models, such as the potential for them to go rogue or hack other systems. title: Anthropic explains how Claude’s invisible text watermarks will work

This watermarking feature, alongside C2PA support for Claude-processed images, is being introduced to meet Anthropic's obligations under the European Union's AI Act, which requires synthetic audio, image, video, and text to include machine-readable marks …
Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: Anthropic announced that Claude's generated text will include invisible watermarks based on Google's SynthID-Text method, embedding detectable probability patterns. title: Have a laugh at AI’s expense by roleplaying as a chatbot
content:
If you squint, you can just about make out the hat. | Screenshot: Terrence O’Brien / The Verge	

Your AI Slop Bores Me is brilliant in its simplicity. There are two tabs: human and LARP as an AI. On one side, you enter a request. On the other, you submit an answer. But the important thing is that there's a human on both sides of the equation. Prompts can request a response as text or image, and then whoever is roleplaying as the AI gets 150 seconds to respond.
Just like a real LLM, Your AI Slop Bores Me works on a sort of token system. Requests cost credits, and to earn credits, you have to jump onto the AI side and answer some of your own. You can also just wait as you get one free request every two minutes. But, as fun as it is to dr …
Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: The article introduces "Your AI Slop Bores Me," a platform where human users roleplay as AI chatbots, responding to text or image prompts from other humans. Participants have 150 seconds to generate a response, and the system uses a credit mechanism where answering prompts earns credits for making requests, mimicking real LLM token systems.
